## claude.ai Todoist

## Todoist Task and Project Management Tools

You have access to comprehensive Todoist management tools for personal productivity and team collaboration. Use these tools to help users manage tasks, projects, sections, comments, and assignments effectively.

### Core Capabilities:
- Create, update, complete, and search tasks with rich metadata (priorities, due dates, durations, assignments)
- Manage projects and sections with flexible organization
- Handle comments and collaboration features
- Bulk assignment operations for team workflows
- Get overviews and insights about workload and progress

### Choosing between tools

What each tool does and how to fill its parameters is in the tool's own description and input schema. This section covers only what those cannot: which tool to reach for, and how tools relate to each other.

**Dates**

- To move a task to a different date use **reschedule-tasks**, never **update-tasks**. update-tasks replaces the whole due string, which destroys recurrence on recurring tasks.
- Never send a task's existing projectId, sectionId or parentId back to **update-tasks** — those fields are treated as a move.
- All dates respect the user's timezone.

**Finding things**

- For "what did I complete?", call **user-info** for the asker's user ID, then **find-activity** with objectType="task", eventType="completed", initiatorId, and dateFrom/dateTo. Without initiatorId the answer covers every collaborator. find-activity reports completion events, including each occurrence of a recurring task; **find-completed-tasks** lists completed tasks, which is not the same question.
- To resolve a person's name or email to a user ID, or to answer "who is X?", use **find-project-collaborators** with just a searchTerm. It covers every shared project you can access plus yourself, so an empty result means they collaborate on none of them — not that they do not exist.

- capture: Capture a new GitHub issue for the isthmia repo with the correct type label, priority, and a clear Problem/Fix body. Use when the user wants to file an issue, log a bug, or record a TODO ("capture this", "file an issue", "make an issue for X").
- triage: Triage open GitHub issues in the isthmia repo — ensure each has a type + priority label, find duplicates/overlaps, flag unclear issues, and recommend close/rescope. Use when the user asks to triage, review the issue backlog, or clean up issues.
- work-backlog: Orchestrate working through the isthmia issue backlog — triage, pick the highest-priority actionable issue, and delegate it to a sub-agent that runs the work-issue workflow. Handles one issue at a time (no parallel work). Use when the user says to work the backlog, work through issues, or "orchestrate issues".
- work-issue: Drive a GitHub issue through the isthmia contribution workflow end to end — optional plan approval, branch, tests, implementation, local verification (just ci), PR, review feedback, and cleanup after a human merges. Use when the user says to work on / fix / implement an issue (e.g. "work issue 45", "start on
- claude:issue:create: Report an issue to the ungood/agents plugin marketplace
- claude:plugins:install: Install one or more plugins from the marketplace into project settings
- github:create-issue: Create a GitHub issue in the current repository using templates
- github:quick-issue: Create a GitHub issue quickly using conversation context
- cli:tldr: Look up concise command-line help using the tldr-pages project
- cli:tree: Show directory structure as a tree visualization
- github:gh-issue: Manages GitHub issues using the gh CLI with commands for creating, listing, viewing, and updating issues
- markdown:markdown: Markdown formatting conventions — heading/list/emphasis style, frontmatter, and link format (aligned with rumdl linter config)
- writing-style:writing-style: Enforces clear, human writing style. Load this skill for all writing — journal entries, summaries, vault notes, and conversational output.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

Isthmia is a collection of TypeScript packages for managing CYC Community Sailing Center operations, built as a pnpm monorepo. The system integrates with Clubspot (a sailing club management platform), Google Workspace, and deploys automated jobs to Google Cloud Platform.

## Development Environment

This project uses a **Nix flake** (with flake-parts) for reproducible development environments. All development commands should be run within the dev shell:

- Enter shell manually: `nix develop`
- Or use direnv to automatically load the environment: `direnv allow`

The dev shell provides:

- Node.js 22 with pnpm (via corepack)
- just (command runner)
- pulumi (infrastructure as code)
- google-cloud-sdk
- gam (Google Workspace admin tool)
- Pre-commit hooks via git-hooks.nix (treefmt for formatting, eslint for linting)

## Common Commands

Use `just` for all common tasks:

- `just` - List all available commands
- `just check` - Run formatting and linting checks
- `just build` - Build all packages using pnpm
- `just clean` - Clean all build artifacts
- `just ci` - Run full CI pipeline (check + build)
- `just deploy` - Deploy to GCP (requires authorization)

- `just test` - Run tests with vitest

### Package-specific Commands

Individual packages can be built using standard pnpm workspace commands:

- `pnpm run build` - Build all packages
- `pnpm run -r build` - Build all packages recursively
- `pnpm run clean` - Clean build artifacts

Each package uses TypeScript with `tsc --build` for compilation.

## Architecture

### Package Structure

The monorepo contains 7 packages organized as follows:

```
packages/
├── commodore/           # Shared CLI utilities (winston logging, commander.js helpers)
├── gsuite/              # Domain-agnostic wrappers around Google Workspace APIs
├── clubspot-sdk/        # TypeScript SDK for TheClubSpot API
├── admin-functions/     # Business logic for reports and data processing
├── todo-manager/        # CLI tool for syncing Todoist tasks
├── calendar-sync/       # CLI tool and library for syncing Google Calendar with Sheets
└── infrastructure/      # Pulumi-based GCP deployment configuration
```

### Dependency Graph

```
commodore (base utilities)
    ↑
    ├── clubspot-sdk (Parse SDK wrapper for TheClubSpot API)
    │       ↑
    │       ├── admin-functions (reports, participants, camps, sessions)
    │       └── todo-manager (Todoist integration)
    │
gsuite (Google Workspace API wrappers)
    ↑
    ├── admin-functions (uses spreadsheet abstractions)
    └── calendar-sync (uses Calendar & Spreadsheet clients)

infrastructure (deploys admin-functions as Cloud Run jobs)
```

### Key Components

**commodore**: Foundation package providing shared CLI and logging utilities. Uses commander-js for CLI parsing and winston for structured logging. Other CLI tools should depend on this for consistent logging and error handling.

**gsuite**: Domain-agnostic wrappers around Google Workspace APIs. Provides:

- `CalendarClient` - Google Calendar API wrapper with CRUD operations for events
- `SpreadsheetClient`, `Spreadsheet`, `Worksheet`, `Table` - Typed abstractions for Google Sheets with rate limiting
- `safeCall` - Rate-limited API call wrapper with exponential backoff retry
- Common utilities like `extractSpreadsheetId`

**clubspot-sdk**: SDK for interacting with TheClubSpot API (a Parse-based backend). The `Clubspot` class handles authentication and provides typed access to cloud functions and queries. Parse SDK is used under the hood with unsafe current user enabled for authentication state.

**admin-functions**: Contains business logic for generating reports about participants, registrations, camps, and sessions. Exports functions that can be invoked as Cloud Run jobs. Uses gsuite package for Google Sheets operations and Google Chat webhooks for notifications. The `runner.ts` module (`ReportRunner`) reads a config spreadsheet ("Reports" worksheet) and runs each enabled row; `reports.ts` defines the abstract `Report` base class and each report subclass registers in the `reports` map. This is the entry point deployed as the `run-reports-job` Cloud Run job.

**todo-manager**: CLI tool that syncs tasks from TheClubSpot (camp schedules) to Todoist. Uses the Doist Todoist API TypeScript client.

**calendar-sync**: CLI tool and library for syncing between Google Calendar and Google Spreadsheet. Can be used as a standalone library or invoked via CLI. Uses gsuite package for Calendar and Spreadsheet operations. Supports one-way sync in either direction with human-readable spreadsheet column headers.

**infrastructure**: Pulumi infrastructure-as-code that deploys admin-functions as containerized Cloud Run jobs on GCP. Creates:

- Docker images in GCP Artifact Registry
- Cloud Run jobs for running reports
- Service accounts with appropriate IAM roles
- Secret Manager secrets for Clubspot credentials

### Authentication

There are two independent auth systems. Do not confuse them.

#### Access policy (least privilege)

Root-level control of the GCP project and Google Workspace is reserved for the two Workspace
super-admin accounts, `master@cyccommunitysailing.org` and `commander@cyccommunitysailing.org`
(only `master@` exists today; `commander@` is planned as a second break-glass admin so root access
is never held by a single account). Those accounts are the only ones used for **configuration**
changes — org policy, project-root IAM, enabling services by hand, Workspace settings.

Individuals (e.g. `ungood@onetrue.name`) are granted only the narrower rights they need to test and
deploy: deploy permissions plus the ability to **impersonate service accounts** (never to log in as,
or hold the credentials of, the super-admin accounts). Day-to-day development and deploys therefore
run as your own account impersonating a service account — not as an admin. New principals default to
no access; grants are added deliberately in `packages/infrastructure/src/config.ts`.

#### Google Cloud (Sheets, Calendar, deploys)

Google APIs use **two different credential types** for **two different purposes**:

| Purpose                                                                    | Credential                                | Command                                                     | Used by                                              |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Deploying (`just deploy`)                                                  | **User credentials**                      | `gcloud auth login` (→ `just auth-gcp`)                     | the `gcloud`, `pulumi`, and `docker` CLIs themselves |
| Running tools locally (`calendar-sync`, `admin-functions`, `todo-manager`) | **Application Default Credentials (ADC)** | `gcloud auth application-default login` (→ `just auth-adc`) | the Node.js `google-auth-library` inside the tools   |

**Which account:** Use your own account (`ungood@onetrue.name`) for `gcloud auth login`. It is granted deploy and impersonation rights in `packages/infrastructure/src/config.ts`. Do **not** log in as `master@cyccommunitysailing.org` for development.

**Which service account:** The deployed job runs as `report-runner@cyc-admin-scripts.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. To make local runs behave exactly like production (same permissions on the same spreadsheets), run tools by **impersonating that service account** via ADC — this is what `just auth-adc` does. This avoids "works locally but not in prod" surprises caused by your personal account having different sheet access.

> Note: the legacy `admin-scripts-runner@` service account still exists in GCP but is no longer used by any recipe. Its deletion is tracked separately in issue #58.

Alternatively, `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` can point at a service-account key file, but impersonation is preferred (no long-lived keys).

#### TheClubSpot (Parse backend)

Separate from Google. The system authenticates to TheClubSpot with a username/password:

1. Locally: supplied via `CLUBSPOT_EMAIL` / `CLUBSPOT_PASSWORD` env vars (or `-u`/`-p` flags — prefer env vars so the password is not visible in `ps`). In production: read from GCP Secret Manager secrets `clubspot-username` / `clubspot-password`.
2. Parse SDK is initialized with TheClubSpot's server URL and app ID.
3. User is looked up by email, then logged in with username/password.
4. Parse SDK's "unsafe current user" mode stores the session in memory (required for subsequent authenticated calls; see `Parse SDK Caveat` below).

## Deployment

Deployment to GCP requires:

1. GCP authentication as a deployer: `just auth-gcp` (`gcloud auth login`)
2. Access to the `cyc-admin-scripts` GCP project (granted in `config.ts`)
3. Run `just deploy` from repository root

Note: the image push no longer needs `gcloud auth configure-docker`. The Pulumi config in `run-reports-job.ts` authenticates the registry push with an OAuth2 access token minted from the running credentials (see the `registries` block), which also works when building through podman. `just deploy` starts a podman machine and points `DOCKER_HOST` at podman's socket.

The deployment:

- Builds all TypeScript packages
- Creates Docker images for admin-functions
- Pushes images to GCP Artifact Registry (us-west1)
- Updates Cloud Run jobs via Pulumi

## Testing

- Tests run with **vitest**: `just test` (or `vitest run`, or `vitest` for watch mode).
- Test files live at `packages/*/test/**/*.test.ts` (see `vitest.config.ts` `include`). Note this is a top-level `test/` directory per package, not co-located `.test.ts` files.
- Current coverage is thin: only `packages/gsuite/test/spreadsheet.test.ts` exists. It uses hand-rolled mock worksheets (no live Google API). New unit tests should follow that pattern — mock the external SDK boundary (Parse, google-spreadsheet, googleapis) and test pure logic.
- `just ci` runs `install → build → check → test`, matching the GitHub Actions `pr.yml` workflow.

## Code Style

- TypeScript with strict type checking (uses `@tsconfig/strictest`)
- ESLint with Prettier integration
- Pre-commit hooks enforce formatting and linting
- All packages use ESM (`"type": "module"`)
- Import paths use `.js` extension (TypeScript ESM convention)

## Important Technical Details

- **Parse SDK Caveat**: The clubspot-sdk enables `Parse.User.enableUnsafeCurrentUser()` to maintain authentication state. This is required for the Parse SDK to work correctly with subsequent API calls.
- **Engine Constraint**: `clubspot-sdk` declares `engines.node: ">= 20.8 < 21"` and `calendar-sync` declares `">= 20.8 < 23"`, but flake.nix (and the Docker base image) provide Node.js 22. The `< 21` bound on clubspot-sdk conflicts with the actual runtime; it is not currently enforced (no `engine-strict` in `.npmrc`) but should be widened to include 22 to avoid confusion.
- **Package Linking**: Some packages have self-references via `link:` in dependencies (e.g., `"@cyc-seattle/admin-functions": "link:"`) - these appear to be for local development
- **Security Overrides**: Root package.json includes pnpm overrides for security vulnerabilities in transitive dependencies

- [Isthmia cleanup initiative](isthmia-cleanup-initiative.md) — testing + auth simplification + bug fixes before new features; two SAs (report-runner vs legacy admin-scripts-runner)
- [Nix devshell uses GNU coreutils](nix-devshell-gnu-coreutils.md) — macOS but Nix provides GNU sed/date; use GNU syntax (`sed -i "..."`, not BSD `sed -i ''`)
- [Platform foundation decisions](platform-foundation-decisions.md) — epic #64: single NixOS VM (Tier B ~$63/mo), Cloud SQL Postgres for Directus/Listmonk/FreeScout, domains, stack renamed prod, human-gated apply
- [Pulumi class-based pattern](pulumi-class-based-pattern.md) — author GCP resources as subclasses with secure defaults + grant methods; don't create resources until needed
- [Helpdesk tool selection](helpdesk-tool-selection.md) — FreeScout confirmed (SLA/reporting needed, collab-inbox limits hit); NO free Workspace: CSC pays Business Standard nonprofit $4.20/user (free tier lacks shared-drive access limits — don't suggest downgrade); mail source open: ~$50–70/mo licenses vs self-hosted mailboxes + Group front doors + SES
- [FreeScout mailbox options](freescout-mailbox-options.md) — DECIDED 2026-08-02: 1 Workspace seat, single shared inbox; outside assignees = free FreeScout users replying to notification emails (no login); a Google Group can't back a mailbox
- [Portal is a Google-auth POC](portal-public-no-auth.md) — cycsail.team portal (#82): static link site, NO app backend, gated by oauth2-proxy on all@; LIVE 2026-08-02 after boot-chain fixes; open item: cross-domain members need direct all@ membership or subgroup flags
- [Google group-membership API limits](google-group-membership-api-limits.md) — hasMember resolves nesting in-domain only; oauth2-proxy falls back to direct-only for cross-domain; checkTransitiveMembership needs Enterprise/CI Premium (CSC is Business Standard); DWD-via-ADC needs SA tokenCreator on itself

```
    │       ├── admin-functions (reports, participants, camps, sessions)
    │       └── todo-manager (Todoist integration)
    │
gsuite (Google Workspace API wrappers)
    ↑
    ├── admin-functions (uses spreadsheet abstractions)
    └── calendar-sync (uses Calendar & Spreadsheet clients)

infrastructure (deploys admin-functions as Cloud Run jobs)
```

### Key Components

**commodore**: Foundation package providing shared CLI and logging utilities. Uses commander-js for CLI parsing and winston for structured logging. Other CLI tools should depend on this for consistent logging and error handling.

**gsuite**: Domain-agnostic wrappers around Google Workspace APIs. Provides:

- `CalendarClient` - Google Calendar API wrapper with CRUD operations for events
- `SpreadsheetClient`, `Spreadsheet`, `Worksheet`, `Table` - Typed abstractions for Google Sheets with rate limiting
- `safeCall` - Rate-limited API call wrapper with exponential backoff retry
- Common utilities like `extractSpreadsheetId`

**clubspot-sdk**: SDK for interacting with TheClubSpot API (a Parse-based backend). The `Clubspot` class handles authentication and provides typed access to cloud functions and queries. Parse SDK is used under the hood with unsafe current user enabled for authentication state.

**admin-functions**: Contains business logic for generating reports about participants, registrations, camps, and sessions. Exports functions that can be invoked as Cloud Run jobs. Uses gsuite package for Google Sheets operations and Google Chat webhooks for notifications. The `runner.ts` module (`ReportRunner`) reads a config spreadsheet ("Reports" worksheet) and runs each enabled row; `reports.ts` defines the abstract `Report` base class and each report subclass registers in the `reports` map. This is the entry point deployed as the `run-reports-job` Cloud Run job.

**todo-manager**: CLI tool that syncs tasks from TheClubSpot (camp schedules) to Todoist. Uses the Doist Todoist API TypeScript client.

**calendar-sync**: CLI tool and library for syncing between Google Calendar and Google Spreadsheet. Can be used as a standalone library or invoked via CLI. Uses gsuite package for Calendar and Spreadsheet operations. Supports one-way sync in either direction with human-readable spreadsheet column headers.

**infrastructure**: Pulumi infrastructure-as-code that deploys admin-functions as containerized Cloud Run jobs on GCP. Creates:

- Docker images in GCP Artifact Registry
- Cloud Run jobs for running reports
- Service accounts with appropriate IAM roles
- Secret Manager secrets for Clubspot credentials

### Authentication

There are two independent auth systems. Do not confuse them.

#### Access policy (least privilege)

Root-level control of the GCP project and Google Workspace is reserved for the two Workspace
super-admin accounts, `master@cyccommunitysailing.org` and `commander@cyccommunitysailing.org`
(only `master@` exists today; `commander@` is planned as a second break-glass admin so root access
is never held by a single account). Those accounts are the only ones used for **configuration**
changes — org policy, project-root IAM, enabling services by hand, Workspace settings.

Individuals (e.g. `ungood@onetrue.name`) are granted only the narrower rights they need to test and
deploy: deploy permissions plus the ability to **impersonate service accounts** (never to log in as,
or hold the credentials of, the super-admin accounts). Day-to-day development and deploys therefore
run as your own account impersonating a service account — not as an admin. New principals default to
no access; grants are added deliberately in `packages/infrastructure/src/config.ts`.

#### Google Cloud (Sheets, Calendar, deploys)

Google APIs use **two different credential types** for **two different purposes**:

| Purpose                                                                    | Credential                                | Command                                                     | Used by                                              |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Deploying (`just deploy`)                                                  | **User credentials**                      | `gcloud auth login` (→ `just auth-gcp`)                     | the `gcloud`, `pulumi`, and `docker` CLIs themselves |
| Running tools locally (`calendar-sync`, `admin-functions`, `todo-manager`) | **Application Default Credentials (ADC)** | `gcloud auth application-default login` (→ `just auth-adc`) | the Node.js `google-auth-library` inside the tools   |

**Which account:** Use your own account (`ungood@onetrue.name`) for `gcloud auth login`. It is granted deploy and impersonation rights in `packages/infrastructure/src/config.ts`. Do **not** log in as `master@cyccommunitysailing.org` for development.

**Which service account:** The deployed job runs as `report-runner@cyc-admin-scripts.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. To make local runs behave exactly like production (same permissions on the same spreadsheets), run tools by **impersonating that service account** via ADC — this is what `just auth-adc` does. This avoids "works locally but not in prod" surprises caused by your personal account having different sheet access.

> Note: the legacy `admin-scripts-runner@` service account still exists in GCP but is no longer used by any recipe. Its deletion is tracked separately in issue #58.

Alternatively, `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` can point at a service-account key file, but impersonation is preferred (no long-lived keys).

#### TheClubSpot (Parse backend)

Separate from Google. The system authenticates to TheClubSpot with a username/password:

1. Locally: supplied via `CLUBSPOT_EMAIL` / `CLUBSPOT_PASSWORD` env vars (or `-u`/`-p` flags — prefer env vars so the password is not visible in `ps`). In production: read from GCP Secret Manager secrets `clubspot-username` / `clubspot-password`.
2. Parse SDK is initialized with TheClubSpot's server URL and app ID.
3. User is looked up by email, then logged in with username/password.
4. Parse SDK's "unsafe current user" mode stores the session in memory (required for subsequent authenticated calls; see `Parse SDK Caveat` below).

## Deployment

Deployment to GCP requires:

1. GCP authentication as a deployer: `just auth-gcp` (`gcloud auth login`)
2. Access to the `cyc-admin-scripts` GCP project (granted in `config.ts`)
3. Run `just deploy` from repository root

Note: the image push no longer needs `gcloud auth configure-docker`. The Pulumi config in `run-reports-job.ts` authenticates the registry push with an OAuth2 access token minted from the running credentials (see the `registries` block), which also works when building through podman. `just deploy` starts a podman machine and points `DOCKER_HOST` at podman's socket.

The deployment:

- Builds all TypeScript packages
- Creates Docker images for admin-functions
- Pushes images to GCP Artifact Registry (us-west1)
- Updates Cloud Run jobs via Pulumi

## Testing

- Tests run with **vitest**: `just test` (or `vitest run`, or `vitest` for watch mode).
- Test files live at `packages/*/test/**/*.test.ts` (see `vitest.config.ts` `include`). Note this is a top-level `test/` directory per package, not co-located `.test.ts` files.
- Current coverage is thin: only `packages/gsuite/test/spreadsheet.test.ts` exists. It uses hand-rolled mock worksheets (no live Google API). New unit tests should follow that pattern — mock the external SDK boundary (Parse, google-spreadsheet, googleapis) and test pure logic.
- `just ci` runs `install → build → check → test`, matching the GitHub Actions `pr.yml` workflow.

## Code Style

- TypeScript with strict type checking (uses `@tsconfig/strictest`)
- ESLint with Prettier integration
- Pre-commit hooks enforce formatting and linting
- All packages use ESM (`"type": "module"`)
- Import paths use `.js` extension (TypeScript ESM convention)

## Important Technical Details

- **Parse SDK Caveat**: The clubspot-sdk enables `Parse.User.enableUnsafeCurrentUser()` to maintain authentication state. This is required for the Parse SDK to work correctly with subsequent API calls.
- **Engine Constraint**: `clubspot-sdk` declares `engines.node: ">= 20.8 < 21"` and `calendar-sync` declares `">= 20.8 < 23"`, but flake.nix (and the Docker base image) provide Node.js 22. The `< 21` bound on clubspot-sdk conflicts with the actual runtime; it is not currently enforced (no `engine-strict` in `.npmrc`) but should be widened to include 22 to avoid confusion.
- **Package Linking**: Some packages have self-references via `link:` in dependencies (e.g., `"@cyc-seattle/admin-functions": "link:"`) - these appear to be for local development
- **Security Overrides**: Root package.json includes pnpm overrides for security vulnerabilities in transitive dependencies

content.content:
1	---
2	tags: [architecture, infrastructure, self-hosted]
3	---
4	
5	## Self-hosted platform architecture
6	
7	This describes a self-hosted operations platform for CYC Community Sailing Center, built on the GCP project
8	(`cyc-admin-scripts`, `us-west1`) and Pulumi setup this repo already uses. It starts from infrastructure — where
9	things run, the database, identity, backups, monitoring — then layers on the Clubspot sync and the CRM (people hub)
10	as the first two applications.
11	
12	The guiding split: adopt maintained software for the hard, security-critical parts (login, the permission engine,
13	the database, backups), and write org-specific glue on top of their APIs. Clubspot stays the registration source of
14	truth for now; the CRM is a derived, enriched store that everything else reads from.
15	
16	Data model and table-level design are deliberately out of scope here — those belong in a design doc.
17	
18	### Principles
19	
20	- One source of truth per fact. Clubspot owns registration-time data; the CRM owns the org-wide view of people.
21	- Everything rebuildable from git. Infra in Pulumi, host config declarative, secrets in Secret Manager — never a
22	  hand-configured box only one person understands.
23	- Least privilege by default, because this platform holds minors' medical and emergency data.
24	- Authorization is relationship-based, not just role-based. What you can see depends on how you relate to a record —
25	  a guardian to their minor, a coach to their event.
26	- Small bespoke surface. Generate the glue; run maintained platforms for the load-bearing pieces.
27	- Extend existing patterns (Cloud Run Job + Scheduler + Secret Manager + `GoogleChatNotifier`) instead of inventing
28	  new ones.
29	
30	### Target topology
31	
32	```text
33	                         Cloud DNS  ──►  TLS endpoint (Caddy on a VM, or Cloud Run domain mapping)
34	                                          │
35	                          ┌───────────────▼────────────────┐

truth for now; the CRM is a derived, enriched store that everything else reads from.

- One source of truth per fact. Clubspot owns registration-time data; the CRM owns the org-wide view of people.

  hand-configured box only one person understands.

  a guardian to their minor, a coach to their event.

content.text:
## What I found

The SDK today (`packages/clubspot-sdk`) only covers registration/billing objects — `clubs`, `camps`, `campClasses`, `campSessions`, `registrations`, `participants`, `billing_registration`, `carts`, `customers`, etc. Nothing for **Events** (as distinct from Camps), **Communication**, **e-signatures**, or general **Accounting/Reporting**. It's built on a clean, extensible pattern:

- `types.ts` — `Parse.Object` subclasses registered via a `@register` decorator, just typed attribute interfaces over Clubspot's raw class names.
- `queries.ts` / `functions.ts` — read-style query builders and `Parse.Cloud.run` wrappers.
- `main.ts` — a generic CLI that auto-generates `get`/`list` subcommands for *every* registered class, which doubles as a great tool for validating hypotheses against live data.

I also checked GitHub: **issue #70** ("Sync Clubspot into the people hub") is exactly this initiative, but it's currently scoped narrowly to registrations and is blocked on **#69** (the Directus people-hub schema design). `docs/architecture.md` explicitly defers "Clubspot → hub field mapping" to a design doc that doesn't exist yet. So the SDK expansion you're describing is actually a *prerequisite* for that design doc, not blocked by it — it tells us what data is even available before anyone designs a schema around it.

## Proposed plan

**Phase 1 — Discovery (browser-driven, one dashboard section at a time)**
For each of Events, Communication, e-signatures, and Accounting/Reporting: I drive Chrome (via claude-in-chrome) through that section of the Clubspot dashboard while you're logged in as an admin, reading captured network requests to identify the underlying Parse REST calls — object class names, attributes, and any `Cloud.run` function names the dashboard calls for reports/summaries.

**Phase 2 — Validate against live data**
Cross-check each discovered class/function using the existing `main.ts` CLI (`clubspot <class> get/list`) against your real CSC data, so the typed model reflects what's actually populated, not just what the network tab implies.

**Phase 3 — Extend the SDK (read-only only)**
Add typed `Parse.Object` subclasses to `types.ts`, query builders to `queries.ts` (following `queryCampEntries`'s style), and any needed `Cloud.run` wrappers to `functions.ts` — for get/find operations only, no `.save()`/`.destroy()`. New classes automatically pick up CLI support for free.

**Phase 4 — Tests**
Unit tests for any query builders with non-trivial logic, following the `gsuite` hand-rolled-mock pattern (mock the Parse SDK boundary, no live calls).

**Out of scope for this work**: the sync database itself (#69/#70) — that stays a separate, later effort, but what we learn here becomes direct input to that design doc.

# Capture an Issue

Turn a problem — from the current conversation or the user's description — into a well-formed GitHub issue in `cyc-seattle/isthmia`.

## Steps

1. **Gather the problem.** Pull details from the conversation or ask the user. A good issue needs: what's wrong or wanted, where in the code (`path:line`), and why it matters.
2. **Check for duplicates first.** `gh issue list --state open --limit 100 --json number,title,labels`. If it overlaps an existing issue, tell the user and offer to comment on / rescope that one instead of filing a new duplicate.
3. **Pick a type label:** `bug`, `enhancement`, `documentation`, or `docker`.
4. **Assign a priority label** using the rubric below.
5. **Write the body** using the template below. Reference concrete files as `path:line`.
6. **Create it:** `gh issue create --title "<imperative title>" --label "<type>,<priority>" --body "$(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF)"`
7. **Report** the issue number and URL back to the user.

## Priority rubric (P0–P3)

- **P0 — Critical:** data integrity/corruption, production broken, or a security-critical hole. Work starts immediately.
- **P1 — High:** a significant bug or friction the user hits regularly, with no safe workaround (e.g. auth/tooling breakage).
- **P2 — Medium:** a real improvement or a bug with a workaround (added tests, hardening, moderate bugs).
- **P3 — Low:** cleanup, docs, polish, low-risk nice-to-haves.

## Body template

Keep it tight. Use `## Problem` always; then `## Fix` (bugs) or `## Proposed changes` / `## Scope` (enhancements); add `## Impact` when the "why" isn't obvious.

```markdown
## Problem

<what's wrong/wanted, with `path:line` references and a code snippet if useful>

## Fix

<concrete change; mention adding a regression test for bugs>

## Impact

<why it matters — omit if self-evident>
```

## Conventions

- **Title:** short, imperative, no priority prefix (priority lives in the label). e.g. "safeCall retries non-retryable errors with a 60s delay".
- Labels already exist: `P0`–`P3`, `bug`, `enhancement`, `documentation`, `docker`. Don't invent new ones without asking.
- For bugs, always note that the fix should include a regression test — tests live in `packages/*/test/**/*.test.ts`.
- Cross-link related issues with `#N` and note dependencies ("land #47 first").

input.command:
gh issue create --title "Expand clubspot-sdk with read-only Events, Communication, E-signatures, and Accounting APIs" --label "enhancement,P2" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

`clubspot-sdk` (`packages/clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts`) only covers camp/registration/billing objects reverse-engineered so far: `Club`, `UserClub`, `Camp`, `CampClass`, `CampSession`, `Registration`, `Participant`, `BillingRegistration`, `Cart`, `Customer`, `EntryCap` (plus vestigial golf `Shift`/`Courses` classes CSC doesn't use).

CSC also needs read access to four areas the SDK doesn't model at all: **Events**, **Communication** (messaging/blasts), **e-signatures** (waivers), and **Accounting/Reporting**. These aren't in the code because they haven't been reverse-engineered from the dashboard yet — the underlying Parse object classes and `Cloud.run` function names are unknown.

## Scope

Reverse-engineer the Clubspot admin dashboard (browser network capture) for each of the four areas, then extend the SDK strictly read-only:

- New `Parse.Object` subclasses in `types.ts`, registered via the existing `@register` decorator pattern.
- Read-only query builders in `queries.ts` (following `queryCampEntries`'s style).
- Any needed `Cloud.run` read wrappers in `functions.ts`.
- No `.save()`/`.destroy()` additions — this SDK usage stays read-only.
- Validate each discovered class against live CSC data using the existing generic `main.ts` CLI (`clubspot <class> get/list`) before committing to a shape.
- Unit tests for any query builder with non-trivial logic, following the `packages/gsuite/test/spreadsheet.test.ts` mock-the-SDK-boundary pattern.

## Impact

This is a prerequisite for the people-hub sync epic (#70) and its schema design doc (#69, "Build the people hub CRM on Directus") — it establishes what Clubspot data is actually available (events, comms history, waiver/signature status, accounting/reporting) before that schema is designed. It also unblocks other planned automations that read from Clubspot: Google Groups sync, WhatsApp channel sync, and eventual website automation (cyccommunitysailing.org).

Not blocked by #69/#70, and doesn't block on them either — independent, additive SDK work.
EOF
)"

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__find
entries.description: Find elements on the page using natural language. Can search for elements by their purpose (e.g., "search bar", "login button") or by text content (e.g., "organic mango product"). Returns up to 20 matching elements with references that can be used with other tools. If more than 20 matches exist, you'll be notified to use a more specific query. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

query.description: Natural language description of what to find (e.g., "search bar", "add to cart button", "product title containing organic")

tabId.description: Tab ID to search in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__get_page_text
entries.description: Extract raw text content from the page, prioritizing article content. Ideal for reading articles, blog posts, or other text-heavy pages. Returns plain text without HTML formatting. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

tabId.description: Tab ID to extract text from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
entries.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward".

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_network_requests
entries.description: Read HTTP network requests (XHR, Fetch, documents, images, etc.) from a specific tab. Useful for debugging API calls, monitoring network activity, or understanding what requests a page is making. Returns all network requests made by the current page, including cross-origin requests. Requests are automatically cleared when the page navigates to a different domain. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

tabId.description: Tab ID to read network requests from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

urlPattern.description: Optional URL pattern to filter requests. Only requests whose URL contains this string will be returned (e.g., '/api/' to filter API calls, 'example.com' to filter by domain).

clear.description: If true, clear the network requests after reading to avoid duplicates on subsequent calls. Default is false.

limit.description: Maximum number of requests to return. Defaults to 100. Increase only if you need more results.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page
entries.description: Get an accessibility tree representation of elements on the page. By default returns all elements including non-visible ones. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default. If the output exceeds this limit it is truncated at a line boundary, with a note giving the full size — pass a larger max_chars, or use depth/ref_id to focus on part of the page. Optionally filter for only interactive elements. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

filter.description: Filter elements: "interactive" for buttons/links/inputs only, "all" for all elements including non-visible ones (default: all elements)

tabId.description: Tab ID to read from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

depth.description: Maximum depth of the tree to traverse (default: 15). Use a smaller depth if output is too large.

ref_id.description: Reference ID of a parent element to read. Will return the specified element and all its children. Use this to focus on a specific part of the page when output is too large.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters for output (default: 50000). Set to a higher value if your client can handle large outputs.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp
entries.description: Close a tab in the MCP tab group by its ID. Use to clean up tabs you're done with. Only tabs in this session's group are closable; call tabs_context_mcp first to get valid IDs. If you close the group's last tab, Chrome auto-removes the group — the next tabs_context_mcp with createIfEmpty starts fresh.

tabId.description: The ID of the tab to close. Must be in this session's tab group. Get valid IDs from tabs_context_mcp.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp
entries.description: Get context information about the current MCP tab group. Returns all tab IDs inside the group if it exists. CRITICAL: You must get the context at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Each new conversation should create its own new tab (using tabs_create_mcp) rather than reusing existing tabs, unless the user explicitly asks to use an existing tab.

createIfEmpty.description: Creates a new MCP tab group if none exists, creates a new Window with a new tab group containing an empty tab (which can be used for this conversation). If a MCP tab group already exists, this parameter has no effect.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
entries.description: Creates a new empty tab in the MCP tab group. CRITICAL: You must get the context using tabs_context_mcp at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Tabs you create are yours to clean up: close each one with tabs_close_mcp as soon as you no longer need it, and close any that remain before finishing your task. Leave a tab open only if the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

entries.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__get_network_request
entries.description: Gets a network request by an optional reqid, if omitted returns the currently selected request in the DevTools Network panel. Useful for inspecting request headers (including 'Cookie') and response headers (including 'Set-Cookie' and directives).

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

reqid.description: The reqid of the network request. If omitted returns the currently selected request in the DevTools Network panel.

requestFilePath.description: The absolute or relative path to a .network-request file to save the request body to. If omitted, the body is returned inline.

responseFilePath.description: The absolute or relative path to a .network-response file to save the response body to. If omitted, the body is returned inline.

entries.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__list_network_requests
entries.description: Lists the most recent requests for the target page since the last navigation.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

pageSize.description: Maximum number of requests to return. When omitted, returns all requests.

pageIdx.description: Page number to return (0-based). When omitted, returns the first page.

resourceTypes.description: Filter requests to only return requests of the specified resource types. When omitted or empty, returns all requests.

includePreservedRequests.description: Set to true to return the preserved requests over the last 3 navigations.

entries.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__list_pages
entries.description: Get a list of pages open in the browser.

entries.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__navigate_page
entries.description: Go to a URL, or back, forward, or reload. Use project URL if not specified otherwise.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

type.description: Navigate the page by URL, back or forward in history, or reload.

ignoreCache.description: Whether to ignore cache on reload.

handleBeforeUnload.description: Whether to auto accept or beforeunload dialogs triggered by this navigation. Default is accept.

initScript.description: A JavaScript script to be executed on each new document before any other scripts for the next navigation.

timeout.description: Maximum wait time in milliseconds. If set to 0, the default timeout will be used.

entries.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__new_page
entries.description: Open a new tab and load a URL. Use project URL if not specified otherwise.

url.description: URL to load in a new page.

background.description: Whether to open the page in the background without bringing it to the front. Default is false (foreground).

isolatedContext.description: If specified, the page is created in an isolated browser context with the given name. Pages in the same browser context share cookies and storage. Pages in different browser contexts are fully isolated (useful for clean-slate testing of cookies and authentication).

timeout.description: Maximum wait time in milliseconds. If set to 0, the default timeout will be used.

entries.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__select_page
entries.description: Select a page as a context for future tool calls.

pageId.description: The ID of the page to select. Call list_pages to get available pages.

bringToFront.description: Whether to focus the page and bring it to the top.

entries.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__take_screenshot
entries.description: Take a screenshot of the page or element.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

format.description: Type of format to save the screenshot as. Default is "png"

quality.description: Compression quality for JPEG and WebP formats (0-100). Higher values mean better quality but larger file sizes. Ignored for PNG format.

uid.description: The uid of an element on the page from the page content snapshot. If omitted, takes a page screenshot.

fullPage.description: If set to true takes a screenshot of the full page instead of the currently visible viewport. Incompatible with uid.

filePath.description: The absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory, to save the screenshot to instead of attaching it to the response.

entries.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__take_snapshot
entries.description:
Take a text snapshot of the target page based on the a11y tree. The snapshot lists page elements along with a unique
identifier (uid). Always use the latest snapshot. Prefer taking a snapshot over taking a screenshot. The snapshot indicates the element selected
in the DevTools Elements panel (if any).

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

verbose.description: Whether to include all possible information available in the full a11y tree. Default is false.

filePath.description: The absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory, to save the snapshot to instead of attaching it to the response.

entries.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__wait_for
entries.description: Wait for the specified text to appear on the selected page.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

text.description: Non-empty list of texts. Resolves when any value appears on the page.

timeout.description: Maximum wait time in milliseconds. If set to 0, the default timeout will be used.

Class Schedule:

If you are in a Saturdays & Sundays class – 3:00 PM to 6:00 PM

If you are in a Tuesdays & Thursdays class – 5:00 PM to 8:00 PM (except 4:00-7:00 for Sept. 15 - Oct. 1)

You can find more details about the program here: Adult Learn to Sail Page. If you have any questions before the course begins, don't hesitate to reach out to info@cyccommunitysailing.org.

We look forward to seeing you on the water!

Kind regards,
Jack

Exploration of all four domains is complete. Here's what I found, mapped against the SDK's existing `@register` pattern:

**Events** — new classes: `events` (social events), `regattas`, `event_tags`, `event_subtypes`. Also discovered `registrations` (already modeled) is shared across camps/regattas/events via `eventObject`/`regattaObject` pointers I hadn't captured. Plus 5 read-only calendar aggregation functions (`retrieve_{camps,regattas,social_events,banquets,group_classes}_for_calendar_v2`) — handy for a future Google Calendar/website sync.

**Communication** — new classes: `contact_lists`, `member_tags`, `forms`, `email_templates`, `ses_email_suppression` (bounces/unsubscribes — important to respect before syncing anyone into Google Groups/a newsletter tool), `ses_emails`/`ses_email_events`. Plus cloud functions `retrieve_sent_campaigns` (campaign history + recipient list) and `retrieve_message_stats` (open/bounce counts).

**E-signatures** — new classes: `contracts` (esignatures.com-backed signing records, per-signer status/timestamps) and `waivers` (templates, linked to camps/events/regattas). Confirms `registrations.waiver_status` already in the SDK.

**Reporting/Accounting** — new classes: `chartOfAccounts` (full GL structure), `lineItems` (the transaction-level ledger, richly nested with orders/customers/paymentIntents/payouts), `payouts` (bank deposits), `invoices_membership`, `merch`/`product_subtypes`, `data_views`. Plus `get_line_items_for_channel_summary`, a cloud function giving revenue-by-channel time series — good for a lightweight financial dashboard without re-deriving it from raw line items.

That's roughly 20 new classes/functions on top of the SDK's current ~14. Given the scope, I want to check in before writing code:

This transactions class is the actual double-entry journal—debits and credits per account line, linked to orders and charges, with human-readable account names and transaction types. This is essentially the general ledger data that feeds QuickBooks, exactly what a treasurer needs for reconciliation.

Combined with `qbo_sync_events` and `chartOfAccounts`, this gives a strong read-only "accounting sync" capability for verifying Clubspot's internal ledger against QBO. I have enough now — let me briefly check `accounting_classes`, tax summary, and expenses since those are treasurer-relevant, then wrap up.

---
name: clubspot-api-discovery-issue-90
description: Parse classes/cloud functions discovered via dashboard network capture for clubspot-sdk expansion (issue #90) — Events, Communication, E-signatures, Accounting/Reporting
metadata:
  type: project
---

Reverse-engineered the Clubspot admin dashboard (theclubspot.com, club id `nw6IMf9Bnq`) via chrome-devtools-mcp network capture to find the Parse classes and `Cloud.run` functions backing four areas not yet in `packages/clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts`. Tracked as GitHub issue [[isthmia-cleanup-initiative|#90]] (not yet implemented as of 2026-09-08 — this is discovery only).

**Why:** clubspot-sdk only covered camps/registrations/billing. The user wants read-only SDK coverage of Events, Communication, E-signatures, and Accounting/Reporting to feed a future Clubspot→database sync (Google Groups, WhatsApp, website automation, and per issue #70/#69 the Directus people hub).

**How to apply:** When implementing #90 (types.ts/queries.ts/functions.ts additions), start from this list instead of re-exploring the dashboard. Validate against live data with the existing `main.ts` CLI before finalizing shapes — response shapes below are from live CSC production data on 2026-09-08 and may have drifted.

## Events
- New Parse classes: `events` (social events), `regattas`, `event_tags`, `event_subtypes`.
- `registrations` (already modeled) is shared across camps/regattas/events via `eventObject`/`regattaObject` pointers, not just `campObject` — SDK's `RegistrationAttributes` needs those added.
- Calendar view uses 5 read-only cloud functions, each `{club_id, start_timestamp, end_timestamp, is_admin}` → lightweight `{id, title, ts, end_ts, type, filter_id}[]`: `retrieve_camps_for_calendar_v2`, `retrieve_regattas_for_calendar_v2`, `retrieve_social_events_for_calendar_v2`, `retrieve_banquets_for_calendar_v2`, `retrieve_group_classes_for_calendar_v2`.

## Communication
- New classes: `contact_lists`, `member_tags`, `forms`, `email_templates`.
- `ses_email_suppression` (bounces/unsubscribes, includes nested `emailObject`/`ses_email_events`) — check before syncing anyone into Google Groups or a newsletter tool.
- `ses_campaigns`, `ses_emails` referenced but only reachable via cloud functions, not direct REST queries: `retrieve_sent_campaigns` (`{club_id, search, skip, limit, status, transactional}` → campaign list incl. full recipient `mdb_search` array — PII, handle carefully) and `retrieve_message_stats` (`{club_id, ses_campaign_ids[]}` → open/bounce/recipient counts per campaign).
- `check_user_can_remove_from_suppression_list` cloud function also seen (read-only check).

## E-signatures
- New classes: `contracts` (esignatures.com-backed; `status` fully_signed/signatures_required, `signers`/`signedByArray` with per-signer sign events and timestamps, linked via `campObject`/`regattaObject`/`membershipObject`/`applicationObject`/`registrationObject`/`waiverObject`) and `waivers` (templates, linked to specific camps/events/regattas via an `events` pointer array).
- No new cloud functions — standard REST queries only.

## Accounting / Reporting
Most relevant for treasurer/bookkeeping use cases:
- `chartOfAccounts` — full GL account list (code, name, accountType, specialType, QBO mapping in `qbAccountObject`).
- `transactions` — **the actual double-entry journal** (this is what "Journal entries" in the nav shows, URL `/accounting/accounting-transactions`). Each row has `lines[]` (debit_acct/credit_acct/amount), `journalsArray` (human-readable account names), `type` (e.g. `order_paid_immediately`, `processing_fees_applied`, `refund_issued`, `invoice_finalized`, `stripe_payout`), linked `orderObject`/`chargeObject`. This is the ground truth ledger — matches QuickBooks after sync.
- `qbo_sync_events` — daily QuickBooks Online sync status log: `{start_date, end_date, status, number_of_journal_entries, number_of_transactions, succeeded_at}`. CSC auto-syncs daily at ~3am. Exactly what's needed to build a "did last night's QBO sync succeed" check.
- `payouts` — Stripe payout records (amount, arrival date, status, bank destination last-4).
- `lineItems` — transaction-line-level detail (heavily nested: orderObject → registrationObject/customer/paymentIntentObject/stripeAccount). More granular than `transactions`, ties revenue lines to specific registrations/participants.
- `invoices_membership` — membership billing invoices (separate from camp/event registration billing).
- `vendors` — vendor list for manually-entered expenses.
- `merch`, `product_subtypes`, `data_views` (saved report configs), `accounting_classes` (QBO "Classes" mapping, empty for CSC).
- Cloud functions: `get_line_items_for_channel_summary` (revenue-by-channel time series with comparison period), `getExpensesRunningTotal`, `getTaxSummaryDetails`.
- Note: "Journal entries" and "Accounting sync" are two different things — `transactions` is the ledger itself, `qbo_sync_events` is the sync run log. Both are read-only and both are useful for reconciliation tooling.

Not explored in depth (lower priority, no data or not treasurer-relevant): Statement runs/Statements (CSC has none configured), Minimums section, Departments, Fundraising, Subtype groups, Z-out reports, Report subscriptions, Scheduled reports.

<system-reminder>This memory is 37 days old. Memories are point-in-time observations, not live state — claims about code behavior or file:line citations may be outdated. Verify against current code before asserting as fact.</system-reminder>
1	- [Isthmia cleanup initiative](isthmia-cleanup-initiative.md) — testing + auth simplification + bug fixes before new features; two SAs (report-runner vs legacy admin-scripts-runner)
2	- [Nix devshell uses GNU coreutils](nix-devshell-gnu-coreutils.md) — macOS but Nix provides GNU sed/date; use GNU syntax (`sed -i "..."`, not BSD `sed -i ''`)
3	- [Platform foundation decisions](platform-foundation-decisions.md) — epic #64: single NixOS VM (Tier B ~$63/mo), Cloud SQL Postgres for Directus/Listmonk/FreeScout, domains, stack renamed prod, human-gated apply

content.text:
Deep-dived the Accounting/Reporting section with the treasurer use case in mind. Key finds beyond the earlier summary:

**For balancing the books specifically:**
- **`transactions`** — this *is* the actual double-entry general ledger (what the nav calls "Journal entries"). Every row has debit/credit account pairs, a human-readable `journalsArray`, a `type` (order paid, refund issued, processing fee, invoice finalized, Stripe payout, etc.), and links back to the originating order/charge. This is the ground-truth ledger that ends up in QuickBooks.
- **`qbo_sync_events`** — a daily sync-status log (CSC auto-syncs to QBO every night around 3am). Each entry shows success/failure, journal entry count, and transaction count for that day. This is exactly what you'd want for a "did last night's sync actually run, and did the numbers match" check — something your treasurer could get pinged about via the existing `GoogleChatNotifier` pattern if a sync ever fails or the counts look off.
- **`payouts`** — Stripe payouts to the bank (amount, arrival date, bank last-4) — needed to reconcile Clubspot revenue against what actually lands in the bank account.
- **`invoices_membership`**, **`vendors`**, and a `getExpensesRunningTotal` function — for the manual/non-registration side of expenses.
- **`getTaxSummaryDetails`** and **`get_line_items_for_channel_summary`** — read-only report functions for tax and revenue-by-channel breakdowns.

I saved all of this (across all four domains) to a project memory tied to issue #90, so this reverse-engineering work doesn't need to be redone in a future session.

I'm not aware of further high-value depth to chase here without diminishing returns (I skipped Statements, Minimums, Departments, Fundraising — CSC doesn't use most of these, or they're not relevant to the four target domains). Want me to keep exploring something specific, or move to implementing the SDK additions (Phase 3)?

I'll model ProductSubtype minimally by analogy with EventSubtype's pattern (chartOfAccounts and tax exempt fields), flagging it with a TODO since it's unconfirmed, rather than chasing further diminishing returns. Data views can just be a low-priority stub for now.

I also noticed the Camp class has chartOfAccounts and account_guest_non_member fields in real data that aren't in the current attributes type—worth adding since they connect camps to accounting. Time to stop exploring and start writing types.ts, organized into clear sections.

I'm planning where to insert new domain groups (Events, Communication, E-signatures, Accounting) while updating existing classes—Camp gets the new accounting fields, Registration gets eventObject/regattaObject with campObject becoming optional. I'll declare ChartOfAccounts early, right after Club, so later classes can reference it cleanly rather than relying on forward declarations.

I can add optional eventObject and regattaObject fields even though SocialEvent and Regatta are declared further down, since TypeScript interfaces are erased at runtime and forward references within the same module scope work fine. I'll leave Registration, RegistrationCampSessionAttributes, and Shift/Courses unchanged, then add a new Events domain section covering SocialEvent, Regatta, EventTag, and EventSubtype classes.

Next I'll add a Communication domain section (ContactList, MemberTag, Form, EmailTemplate, SesCampaign, SesEmail, SesEmailEvent, SesEmailSuppression), an E-signatures section (Waiver, Contract), and an Accounting section covering Transaction, QboSyncEvent, Payout, LineItem, InvoiceMembership, Vendor, Merch, ProductSubtype, DataView, and AccountingClass. Since Parse.Object subclasses each register independently at runtime, class declaration order doesn't actually matter for correctness, so I'll just place ChartOfAccounts somewhere sensible before Camp for readability.

I'm forward-referencing ChartOfAccounts as a type in CampAttributes and EventSubtypeAttributes since TypeScript interfaces don't require earlier declaration. Rather than rewriting the whole file, I'll make targeted edits in three stages: adding optional chartOfAccounts fields to CampAttributes, making campObject optional on RegistrationAttributes while adding eventObject/regattaObject, and appending the new domain-grouped class definitions at the end of the file.

Implementation is complete, builds clean, lints clean, and all 53 existing tests still pass.

## Summary

**`types.ts`** — added 20 new registered `Parse.Object` subclasses across the four domains, all read-only additions following the existing `@register` pattern:
- **Events**: `SocialEvent`, `Regatta`, `EventTag`, `EventSubtype`; `Registration` now models `eventObject`/`regattaObject` alongside `campObject` (which is now optional, since a registration belongs to exactly one).
- **Communication**: `ContactList`, `MemberTag`, `Form`, `EmailTemplate`, `SesCampaign`, `SesEmail`, `SesEmailEvent`, `SesEmailSuppression`.
- **E-signatures**: `Waiver`, `Contract`.
- **Accounting/Reporting**: `ChartOfAccounts`, `Merch`, `LineItem`, `AccountingClass`, `Transaction` (the GL journal), `QboSyncEvent` (nightly sync log), `Payout`, `Vendor`, `InvoiceMembership`. `Camp` also now carries its `chartOfAccounts`/`account_guest_non_member` links.

Where I only had partial field confirmation from live data (e.g. `Form`, `EmailTemplate`, `InvoiceMembership`), I left explicit `TODO` comments rather than guessing structure — consistent with the codebase's existing style.

**`queries.ts`** — 6 new query builders mirroring specific dashboard views: `queryRegistrations` (cross-event signups), `queryContracts`, `querySuppressedEmails`, `queryTransactions` (the ledger), `queryQboSyncEvents`, `queryPayouts`.

**`functions.ts`** — 9 read-only `Cloud.run` wrappers: the 5 calendar feeds, `retrieveSentCampaigns`, `retrieveMessageStats`, `getLineItemsForChannelSummary`, `getExpensesRunningTotal`.

Every new class/query/function is get/find-only — no `.save()`/`.destroy()` anywhere, per the read-only requirement. All new classes automatically get `get`/`list` CLI support via `main.ts`'s existing generic mechanism, so you can validate any of them live once you export `CLUBSPOT_EMAIL`/`CLUBSPOT_PASSWORD`, e.g.:

```
npx tsx packages/clubspot-sdk/src/main.ts transactions list -c nw6IMf9Bnq --limit 5
npx tsx packages/clubspot-sdk/src/main.ts qbo_sync_events list -c nw6IMf9Bnq
```

No unit tests were added — like the existing `queryCampEntries`, the new query builders are declarative filter/include chains with no branching logic to test, consistent with current coverage (issue #48 tracks broader test-coverage work separately).

I haven't committed anything yet — want me to commit this, and should it close out issue #90, or would you like to review the diff first?

All green.

## What changed

**Resolved pointer TODOs** using classes we now have:
- `CampClass.productObject` → `Merch`, `.required_waivers` → `Waiver[]`, `.entryFeesArray` → `EntryFee[]` (a new bare stub)
- `BillingRegistration.stripeAccount`, `Customer.stripeAccount`, `Merch.stripeAccount`, `Payout.stripeAccount` → `StripeAccount` (new bare stub)
- `Participant.profileObject`, `Registration.profilesArray` → `Profile` (new bare stub)
- `Registration.superAdmin`/`userObjects` → `Parse.User`/`Parse.User[]`
- `LineItem`/`Transaction.orderObject` → a newly-fleshed-out **`Order`** class (I had a full nested order JSON from earlier capture, so this one got real attributes rather than a bare stub — status, channel, amounts, `lineItemsArray`, links to `Registration`/`Cart`/`Camp`/`Customer`), `.chargeObject` → `Charge` (bare stub)
- `InvoiceMembership.chargesArray`/`paymentIntentObject` → `Charge[]`/`PaymentIntent` (bare stub)
- Added `RegistrationHold` (bare stub) and wired `Registration.registration_hold`/`hold_expires`/`hold_timestamp`, plus `CustomField` (bare stub) for `Camp.customFieldsArray`

**Left honestly unresolved** (no confirmed target class or shape): `CampClass.subclassesArray`, `Registration.members`/`subclassesArray`, `Participant.contactsArray`/`members`/`members_external` — these are typed `unknown[]` with a comment rather than guessed at, since I only ever observed them empty.

**Expanded `Camp`** substantially from the real JSON captured earlier — location fields, the `collect_*` registration-form flags (useful for knowing what `Participant` data a given camp will actually have), `email_welcome`, housing fields, `cloned_from`, `customFieldsArray`.

**Expanded `Customer`** with the Stripe-customer fields seen nested in line items (name, balance, delinquent, stripeCustomerID, etc.).

Every new stub class (`StripeAccount`, `Profile`, `EntryFee`, `RegistrationHold`, `Charge`, `PaymentIntent`, `CustomField`) follows the existing `Shift`/`Courses` no-attributes pattern — registered so `.include()` still deserializes them as typed objects, ready to be fleshed out later once someone needs their fields.

Build, lint, and all 53 tests are clean. Nothing's committed yet — let me know if you want this as one commit or split (original four-domain addition vs. this expansion pass), and whether to close out #90.

input.command:
gh pr create --title "Expand clubspot-sdk with read-only Events, Communication, E-signatures, and Accounting APIs" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

Expands `clubspot-sdk` with typed, **read-only** coverage for four areas of the Clubspot dashboard reverse-engineered via live network capture (see #90):

- **Events**: `SocialEvent`, `Regatta`, `EventTag`, `EventSubtype`; `Registration` now models `eventObject`/`regattaObject` alongside the existing `campObject` (now optional, since a registration belongs to exactly one). Adds 5 read-only calendar-feed cloud functions.
- **Communication**: `ContactList`, `MemberTag`, `Form`, `EmailTemplate`, `SesCampaign`, `SesEmail`, `SesEmailEvent`, `SesEmailSuppression` (the bounce/unsubscribe list). Adds `retrieveSentCampaigns` and `retrieveMessageStats` cloud function wrappers.
- **E-signatures**: `Contract` (esignatures.com-backed signing records) and `Waiver` (templates).
- **Accounting/Reporting**: `ChartOfAccounts`, `Transaction` (the actual general-ledger journal - what the dashboard calls "Journal entries"), `QboSyncEvent` (the nightly QuickBooks Online sync status log), `Payout`, `LineItem`, `Order`, `Vendor`, `AccountingClass`, `InvoiceMembership`, `Merch`. Adds `getLineItemsForChannelSummary` and `getExpensesRunningTotal` cloud function wrappers.

Also fleshes out several existing types (`Camp`, `Customer`, `Participant`, `Registration`, `CampClass`) with fields and pointer relationships that were previously left as `-->` TODO comments, now that the target classes (`Merch`, `Waiver`, etc.) exist. A handful of new bare stub classes (`StripeAccount`, `Profile`, `EntryFee`, `RegistrationHold`, `Charge`, `PaymentIntent`, `CustomField`) follow the existing `Shift`/`Courses` pattern for pointer targets whose own attributes haven't been reverse engineered yet.

`queries.ts` gains 6 new query builders mirroring specific dashboard views (cross-event signups, contracts, suppression list, the GL journal, QBO sync history, payouts).

**Strictly read-only** — no `.save()`/`.destroy()` added anywhere. This is intended as the data source for a future Clubspot → database sync (see #69/#70), and separately gives useful read access for treasurer/bookkeeping reconciliation (comparing Clubspot's ledger against what actually landed in QuickBooks/the bank).

Where field shapes weren't confirmed against live data, they're left as explicit `TODO` comments rather than guessed.

## Test plan

- [x] `just build` - all 8 packages build clean, including `admin-functions` against the now-optional `Registration.campObject`
- [x] `just check` - lint/format clean (no new warnings in changed files)
- [x] `just test` - all 53 existing tests pass
- [x] Every new class/query/function verified against live CYC production data via Chrome DevTools network capture on the Clubspot dashboard (not via the CLI, since local Clubspot credentials weren't available in this environment)
- [ ] Spot-check a few of the new classes against live data with the `clubspot` CLI once credentials are available, e.g. `clubspot transactions list -c nw6IMf9Bnq` and `clubspot qbo_sync_events list -c nw6IMf9Bnq`

Refs #90.
EOF
)"

That confirms it cleanly — `transactions get pOPE6BjwMa` (a real objectId we saw on the dashboard) returns "Object not found," which is Parse's standard way of masking an ACL denial from a genuine missing record. And the `qbo_sync_events` full record matches the `QboSyncEventAttributes` type exactly (archived, clubObject, dateString, end_date/start_date, number_of_journal_entries, number_of_transactions, status, succeeded_at).

Everything else across Events/Communication/E-signatures/most of Accounting is readable as-is.

This matters for the treasurer-reconciliation use case specifically: to actually pull `transactions`/`payouts` data, either this bot user needs `club_finance` (or `club_admin`) added in Clubspot's Staff permissions, or a separate credential with that role is needed. ## Events
- New Parse classes: `events` (social events), `regattas`, `event_tags`, `event_subtypes`.
- `registrations` (already modeled) is shared across camps/regattas/events via `eventObject`/`regattaObject` pointers, not just `campObject` — SDK's `RegistrationAttributes` needs those added.
- Calendar view uses 5 read-only cloud functions, each `{club_id, start_timestamp, end_timestamp, is_admin}` → lightweight `{id, title, ts, end_ts, type, filter_id}[]`: `retrieve_camps_for_calendar_v2`, `retrieve_regattas_for_calendar_v2`, `retrieve_social_events_for_calendar_v2`, `retrieve_banquets_for_calendar_v2`, `retrieve_group_classes_for_calendar_v2`.

## Communication
- New classes: `contact_lists`, `member_tags`, `forms`, `email_templates`.
- `ses_email_suppression` (bounces/unsubscribes, includes nested `emailObject`/`ses_email_events`) — check before syncing anyone into Google Groups or a newsletter tool.
- `ses_campaigns`, `ses_emails` referenced but only reachable via cloud functions, not direct REST queries: `retrieve_sent_campaigns` (`{club_id, search, skip, limit, status, transactional}` → campaign list incl. full recipient `mdb_search` array — PII, handle carefully) and `retrieve_message_stats` (`{club_id, ses_campaign_ids[]}` → open/bounce/recipient counts per campaign).
- `check_user_can_remove_from_suppression_list` cloud function also seen (read-only check).

## E-signatures
- New classes: `contracts` (esignatures.com-backed; `status` fully_signed/signatures_required, `signers`/`signedByArray` with per-signer sign events and timestamps, linked via `campObject`/`regattaObject`/`membershipObject`/`applicationObject`/`registrationObject`/`waiverObject`) and `waivers` (templates, linked to specific camps/events/regattas via an `events` pointer array).

- `lineItems` — transaction-line-level detail (heavily nested: orderObject → registrationObject/customer/paymentIntentObject/stripeAccount). More granular than `transactions`, ties revenue lines to specific registrations/participants.
- `invoices_membership` — membership billing invoices (separate from camp/event registration billing).
- `vendors` — vendor list for manually-entered expenses.
- `merch`, `product_subtypes`, `data_views` (saved report configs), `accounting_classes` (QBO "Classes" mapping, empty for CSC).
- Cloud functions: `get_line_items_for_channel_summary` (revenue-by-channel time series with comparison period), `getExpensesRunningTotal`, `getTaxSummaryDetails`.
- Note: "Journal entries" and "Accounting sync" are two different things — `transactions` is the ledger itself, `qbo_sync_events` is the sync run log. Both are read-only and both are useful for reconciliation tooling.

Not explored in depth (lower priority, no data or not treasurer-relevant): Statement runs/Statements (CSC has none configured), Minimums section, Departments, Fundraising, Subtype groups, Z-out reports, Report subscriptions, Scheduled reports.
